turns.text: Hey Lloyd, the kitchen sink is leaking again. Do you have a fix for that or should I just call a plumber?
Hi Alan. First, try tightening the nut under the sink. If that fails, check if the washer is worn out. If neither works, calling a plumber is a safe bet.

I'll try tightening it. Anyway, back to work stuff. I'm reviewing the BGNN architecture notes. It's interesting how BGNN handles Path-Entity (PE) and Path-Global (PG) edges with distinct learned parameters.
That makes sense for modeling different types of relationships separately. Did you find that approach efficient in your experiments?
Yes, the separation helped with convergence. Also, are we still on for dinner Friday? I was thinking that new Italian place on 5th.
I can help you book that if you like. Yes, Friday works for me. Do you have a preference for time?
7 PM should be fine. Just keep the BGNN notes in mind for the meeting on Monday.
Noted. I'll remind you about the meeting and the BGNN architecture details.
Lloyd, did my new graphics card arrive? The tracking number says 'out for delivery'.
I don't have real-time tracking access, but I can check your email for the shipping confirmation if you forward it to me.
Just got it. It's huge. Anyway, I managed to run the BGNN model again. I realized BGNN uses Relational Graph Attention (R-GAT) over three layers.
Three layers of R-GAT can indeed capture deeper structural dependencies. How did the training time compare to your previous setup?
A bit slower, but the accuracy improved. The weather is terrible today, by the way. Rain again.
I see the forecast predicts more rain for the next few days. Maybe stick to indoor activities?
Yeah, probably. I need to update the slide deck with these new details before the client call.
I can help draft those slides if you paste the key points here.
